prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a tiered spatial layout from the camera wearer's viewpoint: the wearer's own two forearms in the lower foreground are brightest and closest (~0.3–0.5 m), extending over a tabletop plane (~0.5–0.8 m) toward a seated man on the left (~0.4–0.7 m) and two seated people across the table in the darker background (~1.0–1.8 m away and ~0.5–0.8 m behind the foreground man). Across frames 1 to 3, the man on the left leans sharply forward and downward toward the small condiment cup held in the camera wearer's hands, causing his head and head-mounted camera rig to turn bright white at ~0.3–0.4 m and occlude the background woman and center tabletop before he retreats back to ~0.6–0.7 m in frames 4 and 5. In frame 5, the depth gradient clearly tracks the camera wearer's right arm reaching further across the table (~0.6 m) to meet the outstretched hand of the woman seated opposite (~1.0 m), keeping the condiment cup, white bottle, and blue bottle on the right within arm's reach of the table occupants. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous 3D distance separation between the leaning man, the wearer's hands, and the background diners immediately quantifiable, though it is unreliable on the man's head in frames 2–3 where extreme proximity saturates to flat white and around thin structures like the small spoon and glasses frames which blur into surrounding depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map partitions the scene into discrete object and person instances: the man on the left (`person`, ~0.4–0.7 m), the camera wearer's right arm in the lower foreground (`person`, ~0.3–0.5 m), the woman across the table (`person`, ~1.0–1.3 m) next to a person in a dark jacket (`person`, ~1.2–1.8 m, with a fourth `person` partially entering on the far right edge in frame 5), background chairs (`chair`, ~1.5–2.5 m), the surface below (`dining table`, ~0.5–0.9 m), the blue water bottle on the right (`bottle`, ~0.8 m), and the small white container near the center (`bottle` or `cup`, ~0.6 m). Across frames 2 and 3, the left man's mask expands rightward as he leans down over the table—facing right toward the held cup rather than looking at the camera wearer—and merges with the camera wearer's left arm while occluding the woman behind him and the background chairs. In frames 4 and 5, as the man retreats left and turns his face away, the `dining table` and background `person` masks reappear while the camera wearer's right arm mask reaches forward to contact the woman's hand mask over the table. While segmentation helps isolate overlapping people and tabletop containers in the cluttered background that blend together in RGB, it is frequently unreliable: it merges the camera wearer's left arm into the left man's `person` mask in frames 1–3, misclassifies the man's head-mounted camera as a `cell phone` (frame 3) and the red sauce bowl as a `donut` (frame 4), and leaves large unsegmented black gaps across the tabletop and left hand.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, isolating the articulated finger and wrist geometry (magenta) of the camera wearer's hands in the lower foreground (~0.3–0.6 m from the camera) and, in frame 3 only, an upper-body skeleton (yellow) near the center of the frame. In frames 1, 2, and 4, only a single magenta hand skeleton is detected—capturing the camera wearer's right hand in frames 1–2 (~0.4–0.5 m away, right of center) and left hand in frame 4 (~0.4 m away, left of center) as both hands stay within arm's reach holding the small sauce cup above the table. In frame 5, two magenta hand skeletons appear side by side as the camera wearer's left hand rests near the lower-left bowl (~0.4 m) and the right hand extends higher and further forward (~0.6 m) toward the woman across the table. While the magenta skeletons reveal precise finger flexion and pinch posture during the handoff that are partially self-occluded in the RGB image, the pose map is highly unreliable for overall scene understanding: it completely misses all three to four other people in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, fails to track both of the camera wearer's hands simultaneously in frames 1–4, and produces a distorted, collapsed yellow torso/head skeleton in frame 3 when the left man leans closely over the wearer's hands.
